problem: Existing navigation, scene-memory and mobile-manipulation systems are optimized in isolation. Stored scene evidence goes stale when objects move, semantic region priors stay high after unsuccessful searches, and geometrically reachable endpoints may be infeasible for manipulation.
motivation: Real long-horizon tasks chain search, disambiguation, approach, manipulation and follow-up goals in scenes that change. An outdated assumption at one stage propagates to later decisions, so scene validity, target belief and interaction feasibility need continual, coupled revision.
key_idea: Formulate long-horizon target navigation as continual inference over a factorized posterior of scene memory, target belief and interaction feasibility, using Bayesian persistence for object memory, exploration-progress negative evidence for region priors, and reachability-optimized base poses with hierarchical recovery.
insight: Treating unsuccessful search as negative evidence and grouping dependent context objects both help on MP3D ObjectNav. Removing exploration progress gives SR 0.412 / SPL 0.154, and removing DA-RPA gives 0.426 / 0.155, versus 0.473 / 0.180 for the full method. Dual-source confirmation matters most for fine-grained goals: dropping egocentric VLM evidence lowers SR from 0.271 to 0.231. In real-world mobile manipulation, removing base alignment or hierarchical recovery lowers SR from 71.7% to 60.0% and 55.0%, and disabling dynamic memory updating hurts the relocated-target subtask.
method: Bayesian persistence memory: builds on OmniMap (YOLO-World + TAP + SBERT, probabilistic voxel fusion). Each instance has a binary latent validity state with an absorbing-invalid Markov prior. Stored surface points are projected into depth, classified as support/empty/occluded, and used in a multinomial likelihood for recursive belief updates. Instances are removed when belief falls below tau_death; movable objects are checked whenever observable and large structures at low frequency.

Hierarchical scene graph: instance nodes (category, embedding, color/material/shape/size attributes, centroid, bounding box, persistence belief, observation count), region nodes from spatial grouping, and edges (on/near/above/below). Predicates are LLM-synthesized geometric functions, generated once and reused.
2D exploration-progress map: cells are Unknown/Observed/Explored, with Explored marked only within the central 50° FOV. Cells are aggregated per region to give exploration progress eta_r.

DA-RPA + Bayesian belief revision: co-occurrence from Visual Genome, weighted by persistence belief. Dependent objects are grouped (rho > tau_dep) and the max is taken per group before Noisy-OR aggregation. The posterior is (1-eta)P / ((1-eta)P + 1-P). Frontier score is lambda*posterior + (1-lambda)*(1-normalized distance).

Dual-source fine-grained confirmation: an LLM parses the query into a query graph once. Constraints (color similarity, WordNet path similarity for material/shape, ordinal size, relation predicates) are matched against a memory subgraph and a GPT-4o egocentric VLM subgraph. Scores are fused with alpha = 1 - exp(-N_obs/N0). An exploration-exploitation transition S_best - beta(1-eta_search) > tau_EE decides when to commit.

Reachability-aware base alignment: an offline IK-sampled reachability score is fitted with a differentiable dual-ellipsoid shell. Base pose (x, y, theta) is optimized by two-stage coarse-to-fine PSO on alignment + target reachability/shell obstacle risk + collision (softplus) energy.
Hierarchical closed-loop recovery: manipulation-level retry (regrasp/re-perception), reachability-level base-pose re-optimization, and task-level memory update and re-search/replan.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) for LLM/VLM; YOLO-World, TAP and SBERT perception; Llama3.2-Vision as an ablation backend
setting.training_data: none (training-free); offline co-occurrence prior from Visual Genome and offline IK reachability shell
setting.observation: posed RGB-D (egocentric); wrist camera for manipulation on the real robot
setting.action_space: frontier-based waypoint selection with optimized base-pose goals; arm grasp/place primitives
setting.privileged: none stated (posed RGB-D with camera pose; no pre-built map)

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 trials per level, 3 levels, lab and home office
numbers.extra: real Go2 + ARX X5; baseline OK-Robot* 53.3%

numbers_note: Dynamic long-horizon simulation results (Gibson/HM3D subtask SR/SPL) were only given in a figure, so they are not included. Real-world dynamic navigation is reported as trial counts (relocated subtask 8/9 successes overall). HM3D-ObjNav/MP3D-ObjNav splits are not stated explicitly; 'val' is assumed from the episode counts.
results: OmniNav, training-free, reaches MP3D ObjectNav SR 0.473 / SPL 0.180 (best baseline InstructNav SR 0.420) and HM3D SR 0.546 / SPL 0.285 (UniGoal 0.545 / SG-Nav/GAMap SPL ~0.25-0.26). On fine-grained HM3D instance navigation it has the highest SR (0.271 vs GLMap 0.225) but lower SPL than GLMap (0.103 vs 0.137). Real-world pick-and-place SR rises from 53.3% to 71.7% over OK-Robot*.
limitations: Depends on the accuracy of VLM perception, depth and camera pose. Scene changes are detected only after the affected region is re-observed.
Fine-grained SPL is lower than the strongest baselines because of confirmation overhead; target confirmation (4.58 s/candidate) and base-pose optimization (2.85 s) plus GPT-4o API calls are costly.
Recovery covers only a limited set of failures; real-world evaluation is small (20 trials per level) and compared only against one adapted baseline.
